q8.answer: Counts live in a shared Redis primary, one counter per customer per window under the key rl:{customerId}:{windowId}, which all 6 gateway instances use. Each counter gets a 120 s expiry (set when count becomes 1), so old windows clean themselves up.

q9.answer: Budget resets when the fixed one-minute window rolls over (windowId = floor(unix_seconds/60) from Redis TIME). A new window means a new counter key starting at zero, and the old key expires after 120 s.

q10.answer: The check and increment run inside a single Lua script on Redis, which executes atomically with no other commands in between. The script increments only if count < limit, so two instances cannot both read 99 and both proceed. The gateway never does a separate read then write.

q11.answer: The Lua script returns secondsToWindowEnd = 60 - (now mod 60), with now as whole seconds from Redis TIME. That is always 1 to 60, and the gateway sends it unchanged as Retry-After.

q12.answer: No retry and no local fallback counter in v1. The gateway forwards the request, emits the ratelimit_store_unavailable metric, and the client gets the backend's normal response with no X-RateLimit-* headers, since the real values are unknown.
